title: Live-streaming of court proceedings - the pros and cons for litigants
p1:
What if your courtroom battle was no longer limited to the four walls of a courtroom?

Live-streaming of court proceedings is changing how people see justice, but it also raises questions many litigants never consider.
p2:
Many believe live-streaming only makes courts more transparent. The surprising part? While it can build public trust, it can also expose sensitive moments of a case to a much wider audience.

For litigants, a court hearing is not just a legal process — it can involve personal stories, business disputes, family matters, and private information.
p3:
Live-streaming can help people understand how justice works and allow greater accountability. It can also discourage misinformation about important cases.

But litigants may worry about privacy, public judgment, or their statements being taken out of context. That is why clear rules about what should and should not be broadcast are essential.

The real question is not whether courts should be visible, but how to balance transparency with the dignity and privacy of those involved.
